fact: The RAMCO (formerly LRRRC) Executive Director said the Commission signed an MoU with the National Identification Registry and the Liberia Immigration Service to enhance identity management and legal documentation for persons of concern, especially refugees opting for integration.

Biometric Update reports, citing an LRRRC statement, that the LRRRC, NIR and LIS signed an MoU under which the NIR is to enrol eligible refugees, including integrated Ivorian refugees, in the National Biometric Identification System and issue biometric Refugee Identification cards.

LRRRC, the Immigration Service and the National Identification Registry signed a tripartite MoU on 25 February 2026 under which NIR captures and verifies refugee biometrics and eligible refugees will be issued biometric Resident Permits and Specialized Refugee Identification Cards.

fact: Executive Order No. 144 says the permanent residency and documentation process for registered former Ivorian refugees will be accelerated and provided at no cost, coordinated by the Ministry of Justice with the Liberia Immigration Service, the refugee commission and UNHCR.
Executive Order No. 144 says eligible vulnerable people, including former refugees, will receive or renew National ID cards at no cost and be enrolled in the Liberia Household Social Registry.
